topic: Sharp disconnected Hall prediction sets for ordinal individual treatment effects. Fix L>=3 and two randomized arms with Y(d) in {0,...,L-1}; the marginals mu0,mu1 are identified and their coupling is unrestricted. For every effect set S define worst-coupling coverage h_mu(S), and define the deterministic shortest valid set by cardinality, span, then binary code. Prove the exact Hall/rectangle representation, characterize all shortest sets, give necessary-and-sufficient disconnectedness inequalities and the complete L=3 frontier, derive sharp general-L bounds comparing shortest arbitrary sets with shortest intervals, and compute them by an explicit min-cut plus finite outer optimization. Use simultaneous multinomial confidence-polytopes to certify every reported set uniformly, with selection consistency on the stated fixed-margin class. Consumer: the seven-category endpoint in Goldman et al.'s remdesivir 5-versus-10-day trial. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact derivation gives h(S)=max(0,max_{A-B subset S}[mu1(A)+mu0(B)-1]), so every cardinality minimizer is a threshold-feasible difference set A-B. The presolve derived a complete L=3 frontier and sharp bounds I*/k* <= (2L-1)/3 and I*-k* <= 2L-4, attained by strictly positive endpoint-heavy marginals for every 0<alpha<1/2. The accepted witness has exact coverage 39/50; 43,560 rational L=3 cases and 120 independent transport comparisons passed. An invalid robust min/max interchange was found and removed; Hall duality is supporting prior art, not the headline. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify the all-minimizer rectangle normal form at boundary marginal laws and the exhaustive L=3 support-pattern classification; numerical checks do not prove the universal statements. EARLY KILL TEST: Compare transport LPs with rectangle selection for every effect set on bounded L=3 and L=4 rational grids, including zero cells and threshold equalities, and verify the endpoint-heavy extremizers; any mismatch stops or pivots the run. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_ite_disconnected_hall_set.md

open_problems.open_problem: For arbitrary ordinal effect sets, does every cardinality-minimal valid set admit a threshold-feasible difference-set representation S=A-B, including zero marginal cells and exact Hall equalities, and which pairs (A,B) represent each minimizer?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing ordinal work treats intervals, individual diagonals, or fixed threshold events, while finite Strassen theory supplies exponentially many Hall inequalities for a fixed allowed support. The missing theorem must reduce the outer optimization over arbitrary effect sets to difference sets and prove the converse for every minimizer. Generic strict-support reasoning does not cover simplex faces: zero marginal cells and exactly binding coverage cuts can change the active neighborhoods and create multiple representing rectangles. Prior CausalSmith constructions prove sharp threshold extrema or fixed-staircase feasibility, but not this optimizer-wide boundary-safe normal form.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-support duality theorem giving h_mu(S) exactly and an if-and-only-if characterization of every cardinality-minimal valid S as A-B, with all admissible representing pairs and explicit clauses for zero masses and binding Hall equalities.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from randomized-arm marginals to robust ITE prediction and stops where arbitrary non-overlapping effect sets begin.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Randomization identifies only potential-outcome marginals -> the ITE law depends on an unrestricted coupling -> interval-only prediction can conceal sharper arbitrary sets -> characterize all shortest coupling-robust supports

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the finite Strassen-Hall equivalence and its combinatorial proof to the complement of the allowed difference relation, then identify minimal Hall witnesses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Worst-coupling coverage is a support-constrained transportation problem, so Hall deficiencies are precisely the dual certificates that must yield the rectangle normal form.

method_exemplars.technique: Extend the cumulative-threshold coupling construction for sharp ordinal benefit bounds from one threshold event to the full family of active subsets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Their endpoint formulas are a one-threshold face of the desired arbitrary-effect-set characterization.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over constrained stochastic-optimization inference and its treatment of optimizers lying on polyhedral boundaries.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The coverage functional is a nonsmooth optimum over the same ordinal fixed-marginal transportation polytope.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Disconnectedness first becomes substantive at L=3, where selection compares all subsets of five possible effects. Existing ordinal bounds cover scalar order events, and prior CausalSmith reviews explicitly identify joint sharpness across benefit tiers as unfinished; coordinatewise extrema cannot certify a common coupling or the selected support. A complete frontier must enumerate Hall-minimal forbidden-edge patterns and then apply the cardinality/span/code rule. Interior computations do not establish exhaustiveness because zero cells, binding thresholds, and tied objectives create lower-dimensional regimes with different active certificates.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite, mutually exclusive, jointly exhaustive system of inequalities in the six marginal masses and the coverage threshold, with each cell listing all shortest valid sets and a necessary-and-sufficient condition for the deterministic selection to be disconnected.

writing_exemplar.why: Its binary marginal-plane phase diagrams are the closest presentation model for an exhaustive ternary frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Binary robust ITE intervals admit a complete marginal-plane classification -> ternary outcomes create five effect values and genuine holes -> classify exactly when the shortest valid support disconnects

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its transportation reductions and constructive sharpness arguments for ordinal order events to every candidate union of effect diagonals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both targets are linear functionals of the same ternary joint-potential-outcome table with fixed marginals.

method_exemplars.technique: Use exact discrete-program enumeration to generate candidate active systems, followed by symbolic dual certificates establishing that the resulting cell partition is exhaustive.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The L=3 frontier is a finite discrete partial-identification problem in which exhaustive computation can expose omitted support regimes before proof.

method_exemplars.why_closest: Frontier boundaries are exactly the points at which active constraints or the selected optimal set change.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A fixed-set transport program computes coverage, but the interval penalty optimizes over two nested combinatorial classes of effect sets and then over both marginal laws. The ordered difference geometry prevents summing pointwise probability bounds or applying a generic set-cover ratio. Existing robust ITE work is interval-only, while structured conformal results concern coverage under an observed response distribution rather than an adversarial potential-outcome coupling. Prior threshold min-cut constructions supply local certificates but no compression theorem comparing arbitrary Hall witnesses with contiguous supports for every L.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Sharp functions c_L and d_L satisfying I*/k*≤c_L and I*-k*≤d_L for all marginal pairs, together with strictly positive attaining families and a characterization of all equality regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames prediction-set efficiency through the exact cost of imposing geometric structure and separates structured from unrestricted optima.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Coverage alone permits irregular prediction sets -> interpretability favors geometrically structured sets -> structure can enlarge the optimum -> quantify the exact price of requiring intervals under unknown ITE dependence

method_exemplars.technique: Use Hall-neighborhood certificates to lower-bound feasible arbitrary supports and construct matching couplings for the interval lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sharp separation requires certificates for both feasible arbitrary supports and infeasible smaller supports, which are the two sides of finite Hall-Strassen duality.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the structured-versus-oracle comparison and extremal-instance proof, replacing empirical probability coverage with worst-coupling Hall coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems compare an unrestricted prediction-set oracle with an interval-structured oracle under a coverage constraint.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate multinomial marginal uncertainty through the competing piecewise-linear transportation optima using constrained-optimization asymptotics.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An empirical interval-price comparison is a difference of nonsmooth optimal values over ordinal transportation polytopes.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The map from the two arm marginals to the lexicographically selected shortest set is discontinuous when coverage constraints bind or minimizers tie, and zero cells place the law on changing-dimensional simplex faces. Existing multinomial regions cover the marginal vectors but do not themselves prove uniform causal-set certification or optimizer recovery; existing ordinal-bound inference targets scalar endpoints. A prior CausalSmith confidence-polytope construction covers transport images at Hall ties, but selection consistency additionally requires a uniform modulus for every candidate set and a positive gap from all feasibility and tie-break boundaries. Honest coverage may remain possible at ties even though exact selector recovery is impossible there.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable confidence-polytope procedure with uniform coverage for every reported effect set, an argmin-selection theorem on an explicit positive-separation class, and a boundary impossibility or conservative-validity result showing why exact recovery cannot be demanded on tie surfaces.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly motivates why sampling uncertainty layered on ordinal partial identification creates a nonregular optimization problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Ordinal causal quantities are only partially identified -> sharp values solve constrained optimization -> sampling changes active constraints -> selected shortest sets require simultaneous boundary-robust inference

method_exemplars.technique: Form finite-sample multinomial simplex regions by test inversion and combine the independently sampled arm regions before optimizing worst-case coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The nuisance parameters are exactly two categorical probability vectors, so their simplex regions provide the outer confidence event needed for uniform certification.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the constrained stochastic-program expansion and conservative treatment of changing or nonunique active sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both procedures optimize causal functionals over fixed-marginal ordinal coupling polytopes and become nondifferentiable at active-set changes.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply directional-delta and bootstrap arguments to the piecewise-linear Hall coverage map while retaining all tied active rectangles.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Worst-coupling coverage is directionally differentiable, whereas the discrete selector changes at tied faces and therefore needs a separate separation argument.

literature_map:
Zhang and Richardson (2025, arXiv:2506.07469) is the closest anchor: it studies robust ITE prediction from randomized-arm marginals, treats binary intervals, gives ordinal pmf bounds, and leaves non-overlapping prediction sets open.
Zhang and Richardson (2024, arXiv:2405.08806) revisit Makarov-Rüschendorf sum bounds and show why atoms and discontinuous outcomes require special care.
Fan and Park (2010, Econometric Theory, DOI 10.1017/S0266466609990168) provide foundational DTE bounds and inference, with later work refining sharpness for discontinuous laws.
Firpo and Ridder (2019, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2019.04.012) distinguish pointwise from uniform sharpness, which matters for multi-effect set coverage.
Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018, JEBS, arXiv:1507.01542) derive sharp ordinal benefit and strict-benefit bounds under fixed marginals, not shortest arbitrary prediction sets.
Lu, Zhang, and Ding (2020, Biometrics, arXiv:1907.10287) give sharp bounds for the ordinal relative treatment effect under unrestricted dependence.
Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024, Biometrika, arXiv:2305.10555) extend symbolic ordinal benefit bounds, confirming the literature's focus on scalar order events.
Koperberg (2024, Statistics & Probability Letters, DOI 10.1016/j.spl.2024.110089) proves the finite Strassen-Hall equivalence underlying support-constrained coupling certificates.
Duarte et al. (2024, JASA, arXiv:2109.13471) automate sharp discrete causal bounds by polynomial programming, useful for computational validation but not a symbolic shortest-set classification.
Huang et al. (2019, Biometrics, DOI 10.1111/biom.13101) show that inference for ordinal coupling bounds is nonregular at polyhedral boundaries.
Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2021, arXiv:2002.01044) construct finite-sample multinomial confidence regions, providing a natural outer layer for two-arm marginal uncertainty.
Caughey, Dafoe, Li, and Miratrix (2023, JRSSB, DOI 10.1093/jrsssb/qkad080) give simultaneous randomization-inference intervals for finite-population ITE quantiles, a complementary inferential target.
Gao et al. (2025, ICML, arXiv:2502.16658) study efficient unions of intervals in conformal prediction; no analogue was located for interval-versus-arbitrary sets under adversarial potential-outcome couplings.
Lee (2024, Journal of Applied Econometrics, arXiv:2108.00723) develops conditional Makarov bounds and uniform inference but does not optimize disconnected ordinal effect sets.
Goldman et al. (2020, NEJM, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2015301) provide the motivating randomized trial and seven-category endpoint; the published analysis compares marginal ordinal status rather than individual-effect prediction sets.
